newsitem.title: UK: Options--Gold OTC vols still weak ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: Options--Gold OTC vols still weak ahead of expiry.

text.p: Volatilities on over-the-counter gold options have crumbled further around historic lows ahead of Wednesday's expiry as sellers pressure a long and stagnant market, dealers said. "There seems to be nothing but sellers. A lot of market makers are long so any buying that comes in is just mopped up by those long positions," a London dealer said.
Ahead of Wednesday's 1330 GMT expiry, open interest on August was scattered at strikes on every dollar and half dollar from $385 to $390, but there were few above $390, they added.
The underlying market is expected to hover around $390, with delta hedging seen on any move above that level, but prices should ease after the expiry, dealers said.

"I think they will have to cover a bit more if it moves towards the $390 level. There is a little bit of buying potential around because of the expiry," a dealer in continental Europe said. "After the expiry, though, I don't think we'll have the support necessary to keep it up."
Option players may be tempted to go short to squeeze out earnings with volatilities at historic low levels, but it would be a risky move, another said.
"You've got to be massively short with the vols at these numbers to earn a crust. Whether people are prepared to take that risk, I don't know," he said.
Near-term implied volatilities have slid nearly 100 basis points over the past two weeks, with September at-the-money options bid around 4.00 percent, dealers said.
"I've even heard of some very short stuff, one to two weeks, trading at 3.5 percent," a London dealer said.
Longer dates, while under pressure, were managing to hold their levels a bit better.
"People are still hoping that we are going to have some movement down the line late this year or early next year. But the short end really gets whacked," a dealer said.
November options were bid at 5.00 to 5.25 percent, February 1997 at 5.75 percent and August 1997 at 7.0 to 7.5 percent.
Implied volatilities were feeling pressure from lacklustre customer interest in a market that was generally long. Historic near-term volatilities hovered around 3.0-4.0 percent.
"You've just got desperate longs and sellers who are getting less and less everyday. It's difficult to get out at the moment," a dealer said.
The silver options market was seeing a bit more speculative interest, but volume was also bumping along at very low levels.
The spot price was hemmed in by the $5.25 and $5.30 strikes, dealers said.
"There may be a few shorts around who will have to start buying if you go above $5.30, that is the goal of the market," one said.
"But if you had a correction on the downside you will see additional selling below $5.25," he added.
Implied volatilities were weak after spiking one to two percentage points last week when spot prices jumped 10-15 cents as speculators sought very short-dated options.
Volatilities later eased back when underlying prices stalled, falling about three points.
Volatilities for at-the-money September options were bid at 14.0 to 14.5 percent, November at 15.5 to 16.0 percent and six-month to one-year dates at 17 to 18 percent.
